title: Chapter 120: Rusted Key
html:
I’ll be fine if I’m careful.

Chen Ge opened his backpack, tucked Xiaoxiao into his shirt pocket, and took out his flashlight and mallet.

“What are you doing?” Hearing the commotion, Doctor Gao emerged from the bedroom. One look at Chen Ge’s peculiar equipment made his head ache.

“You’re just in time.” Chen Ge dragged Doctor Gao to the window. “We’ll keep in contact. You stay in Room 304, and I’ll go take a look in Room 303.”

“Why are you going into Room 303?” Doctor Gao’s gaze moved from the mallet in Chen Ge’s hand to the doll protruding from his pocket. His eye twitched.

“The source of Men Nan’s problem should be inside. I need to investigate before midnight.”

“You plan to go in this get-up? With a doll?”

“I might hesitate if I were alone, but with you backing me up, I’m confident.” Chen Ge called Doctor Gao and slipped the phone into his shirt pocket. “Keep the line open.”

Doctor Gao nodded reflexively, gripping his phone as the burden on his shoulders grew heavier. He was now responsible for the safety of two “patients.”

“Be careful!”

Chen Ge climbed onto the sill, shoved the mallet into his pants pocket, and pressed himself against the wall. Keeping one foot braced in Room 304’s window, he kicked Room 303’s window open with the other.

“Doctor Gao, keep the call connected. If anything happens, get help.” He leaned out and stretched one leg toward Room 303’s sill while keeping his weight over Room 304. Once his foot found purchase, he shifted his grip and slowly transferred his weight toward the neighboring window.

With most of his body suspended before Room 303, he aligned himself with the opening, released his left hand, and seized the sill with his right. One hard pull brought him across.

“Breaking into the neighbor’s apartment to treat a patient?” Doctor Gao wanted to stop him, but Chen Ge had already vanished through Room 303’s window. In more than a decade of practice, he had never encountered anything like this during a diagnosis.

Chen Ge angled himself downward and slid through the opening. I’m in.

Room 303 had remained untouched since the incident. Dust blanketed everything, grime stained the walls, and the floor beneath his feet was uneven. When Chen Ge switched on his flashlight, its beam revealed an old, filthy carpet.

None of the other apartments are carpeted—not even the landlady’s. Why this one?A foul stench seeped from beneath it. Suspicious, Chen Ge seized one edge and tore it back.

At first, he found only a pile of old men’s clothing. The garments were all roughly the same size and probably belonged to one person.

Moldy clothes shouldn’t smell this bad.Using the mallet to push them aside, he uncovered something far more disturbing: several dead sparrows.

The bodies are intact, so they can’t have been dead for more than a week.Mastering the Dollmaker’s Talent had given Chen Ge a rudimentary understanding of corpses. No one has rented this room since the incident, yet someone entered within the past week and hid these birds beneath the clothes.

The discovery complicated matters and sent his suspicions in a new direction.

Wang Haiming died somewhere in this room. I don’t know the exact spot, but if I search everything, I’ll find something.Finding nothing else in the living room, Chen Ge stepped over the clothes and entered the bedroom.

A metal-frame bed leaned against the wall. Several old bookcases stood nearby, a few books still rotting on their shelves. Moisture had covered the pages with mold and filled the room with a peculiar odor.

Chen Ge searched every drawer and cabinet without success, then moved into the bathroom. All the apartments shared a similar layout; when he opened the door, a mirror stared back at him.

Lit only by the flashlight, the reflection scarcely resembled him. He remained outside and inspected the bathroom from the threshold.

There don’t seem to be any other clues.The apartment was small, and he had examined every corner.

Standing in the living room, Chen Ge studied the clothes beneath the carpet. This is strange. They’re all stained with blood, but a few sparrows couldn’t have soaked so many garments.

With the aid of Yin Yang Vision, Chen Ge’s sight was better than most, and he soon discovered something weird.

There’s something wrong with the clothes.

Mallet ready, he examined each garment until he found an ordinary gray jacket at the bottom of the pile. Dried blood covered its shoulder and back. Wang Haiming had probably worn it while smashing his head against the wall; only blunt-force trauma to the skull would produce that pattern of spatter.

What’s this?Something rattled in the pocket when Chen Ge shook the jacket. He reached inside, felt cold metal, and withdrew a rusted key.

The apartment keys are flat and made of copper. This one is much larger.Why would a former psychiatric patient carry a key that did not fit his own door?

Did he find it somewhere? If so, why keep it?Unable to determine its purpose, Chen Ge pocketed it. As he turned to leave, his flashlight swept across the open window. The glass reflected a shadow: the tenant of Room 302 had leaned out to spy on him.

Why does he care that I entered Room 303?Pretending not to notice, Chen Ge replaced the clothes while his thoughts raced. Only someone in Room 302 or 304 could enter through a window. Men Nan is the victim, so the man in 302 probably hid the sparrows here.

But why? Has he been possessed by the creature in Room 303 as well?

He recalled the young man talking to himself and arguing with the wall—behavior disturbingly similar to Wang Haiming’s.
